subject.title: test(tooling): stabilize lifecycle measure pid fixtures

question: Which stubborn-descendant timeout/grace budget should survive the current-main conflict before this test-only stabilization lands?
rationale: The PR's useful non-empty wait is clear, but current main changed the same timeout budget after the PR base; choosing between the faster current budget and the PR's larger startup budget is an owner intent call before merge.

options.title: Rebase with proven timing
options.body: Apply the non-empty waits on current main and choose the smallest timeout/grace budget that still passes the affected Linux tooling shard.

options.title: Accept the PR budget
options.body: Keep the PR's `3000`/`200` fixture budget and accept the slower test in exchange for more CI startup slack.

options.title: Keep current fast budget
options.body: Apply only the non-empty waits while preserving current main's `250`/`50` budget, then require fresh Linux proof that the startup race is gone.

recommendation.title: Rebase with proven timing
recommendation.body: Apply the non-empty waits on current main and choose the smallest timeout/grace budget that still passes the affected Linux tooling shard.
